title: How Jacky built and sold a $190K towing directory using Facebook lead ads and a closer
summary: Jacky bought a high-traffic towing directory that was under-monetized, added a strong sales closer, and ran one Facebook lead ad campaign (about $25 CAD/day) to fill cold leads. Clients got the exclusive #1 slot per city with call forwarding, a guaranteed call volume, and a free trial. He sold it for $190K.

principles.text: Buy traffic-rich sites the owner can't monetize, then out-monetize them with better sales.
principles.quote: I thought I was like, "Okay, this guy has a ton of traffic. He's not monetizing correctly. I could probably outmonetize him.

principles.text: When inbound leads aren't closing, the fix is a great salesperson, not more traffic.
principles.quote: my strategy was immediately hire a cracked sales guy. All right. And then start generating leads.

principles.text: Sell scarcity: one client per city in the #1 slot, priced high because you own the traffic.
principles.quote: we only take one client per city and that was like insane. I think the most we've ever charged per city was like 2.5k per month and that's cuz we had all the traffic

principles.text: Reduce buyer risk with a concrete guarantee and refund the shortfall if you miss it.
principles.quote: guaranteed 50 calls per month. We are the largest towing directory in America.

principles.text: Use a free trial of forwarded leads to close: they get real leads, and you move on if they don't buy.
principles.quote: we would just start forwarding them leads and if they closed great if they don't close we move on to the next person

principles.text: Keep paid acquisition simple: one Facebook lead ad campaign with a short form and a small daily budget.
principles.quote: it was only $25 spent per day and it was that simple. So, the lead campaign was called Meta Leads.
